title: Introductions - Ali Mousa
author: Ali Mousa
excerpt: APL-SURP COSZO intern joining the installation cruise on the R/V Roger Revelle, after a summer huddle-testing the four ocean-bottom seismometers we will deploy.
body:
My name is Ali Mousa. I am an APL-SURP COSZO intern joining the installation cruise on the R/V Roger Revelle.

I am a recent graduate from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee. I have an interdisciplinary background in conservation and environmental science that includes biology, geology, geography, and resource management.

I’ve been honored to complete my first research project with UW-Oceanography under William Wilcock and Maleen Kidiwela, my project was testing for consistency (huddle-testing) between the 4 ocean-bottom seismometers we will deploy later this month. I feel honored and humbled to have partaken in real-world and potentially life saving research. This summer has changed my life, and I look forward to have my first sea-going experience on a research vessel.

I will keep you updated on my adventures at sea,

Stay tuned!

title: Introductions - Yoichiro Dobashi
author: Yoichiro Dobashi
excerpt: Third-year UW Ph.D. student observing seafloor deformation with ocean-bottom pressure gauges — and the new GSSM.
body:
My name is Yoichiro Dobashi, and I’m a third-year Ph.D. student from Japan working with William Wilcock and David Schmidt at the UW School of Oceanography.

I came to UW because I was excited by its cutting-edge seafloor observation technology and the opportunity to work across different fields. Currently, my research focuses on improving the observation of seafloor deformation (from mm to m) using ocean-bottom pressure gauges. These sensors are incredibly versatile—they can capture signals from tsunamis, earthquakes, volcanoes, and even climate-scale ocean variability.

I’m especially excited that an instrument (Geodetic and Seismic Sensor Module: GSSM) we’ve tested through many experiments with the UW APL team will soon be deployed in the field. I can’t wait to see how it performs on the Cascadia subduction zone (CSZ).

Stay tuned!

title: Introductions - Michael Hemmett
author: Michael Hemmett
excerpt: Second-year UW graduate student studying seismology and marine geophysics — excited to set sail on the R/V Roger Revelle.
body:
My name is Michael Hemmett, and I am entering my second-year as a graduate student studying seismology and marine geophysics with Marine Denolle and William Wilcock in UW Earth and Space Sciences!

I am particularly interested in studying the structure and dynamics of volcanoes and subduction zones. Growing up in Washington, I am committed to conducting research in fundamental science and natural hazards in order to advance the well-being of folks in the Pacific Northwest. I use seismic data to study stress evolution at Axial Seamount volcano off the coast of Oregon, where I hope to better understand mid-ocean ridge eruption dynamics and the seafloor spreading cycle.

I can't wait to set sail on the R/V Roger Revelle for next week's COSZO Installation Cruise!
